findings.reason: A real final-only provider stub returned completed task artifacts without any authorized write. A new regression ran red because cancellation wrongly emitted TaskCancelledError. The executor now reuses the existing completed-step semantic verifier before claiming a safe cancellation; the matching test is green and produces an ordinary execution error instead.

Independent first-round review reproduced completed_side_effects refusing the new cancellation field and losing confirmed prefix steps. A named regression ran red before the shared cancellation/budget validators were wired into the legacy reader; current prefix and remaining-step output is verified.

Independent review reproduced completed commands with nonzero exits, timeout=true or disagreeing archive hashes being accepted by report/checkpoint parsers. Six isolated mutations ran red before the pure shared validator added exact exit types/values, timeout and archive consistency checks. Named report/checkpoint regressions now reject all six.

The third bounded follow-up reviewed the previously unreviewed stop_after/model-repair branches and the added cumulative-acceptance/exhausted-or-unknown-usage tests. Seven reviewer in-memory assertions and the author-owned runtime checks close only that named combination scope. R5 was found and closed by explicit early refusal; no fourth complete review or overall product acceptance is claimed.

Independent third-round in-memory probe observed a successful repair retry binding the original failed command archive; cancellation then failed completed-evidence validation. Fixed by early refusal instead of support: supplying cancellation with model_repair=model now raises a fixed TaskExecutionError before artifact reads, provider/command calls or report writes. Two pending/requested owner regressions ran red (2 failures, 0 errors) then green. Reviewer statically closed the four-line guard and two negative tests; original retry evidence behavior without cancellation is not fixed or certified.
